```{r}
# Removing all saved variables
rm(list = ls())
```

```{r}
# Loading processed data set and viewing first 6 rows
heartdisease.final <- read.csv("heartdisease_new.csv")
head(heartdisease.final)
```

```{r}
for (i in 1:12){
  # Looping through each variable making all of them factors
  heartdisease.final[,i] <- as.factor(heartdisease.final[,i])
}
```

```{r}
# Removing the outlier marker variable
heartdisease.all <- heartdisease.final[,-13]
```

```{r}
library(bnlearn)
```

```{r}
# Setting a seed
set.seed(2026)
```

```{r}
# Cross-validation
cv.results.aic <- bn.cv(
  # The data set
  data = heartdisease.all,
  # The hill climbing algorithm
  bn = "hc",
  # Using AIC in hill climbing algorithm
  algorithm.args = list(score = "aic"),
  # Using Bayesian reasoning to estimate probabilities
  fit = "bayes",
  # How much influence the prior has on the fitted probability
  fit.args = list(iss = 2),
  # Loss function for the cross validation (log-likelihood)
  loss =  "logl",
  # Number of folds
  k = 10,
  # Number of times to  repeat the 10-fold cross-validation
  runs = 5
)
# Outputting the cross-validation results
print(cv.results.aic)
```

```{r}
# Cross-validation
cv.results.bic <- bn.cv(
  # The data set
  data = heartdisease.all,
  # The hill climbing algorithm
  bn = "hc",
  # Using BIC in hill climbing algorithm
  algorithm.args = list(score = "bic"),
  # Using Bayesian reasoning to estimate probabilities
  fit = "bayes",
  # How much influence the prior has on the fitted probability
  fit.args = list(iss = 2),
  # Loss function for the cross validation (log-likelihood)
  loss =  "logl",
  # Number of folds
  k = 10,
  # Number of times to  repeat the 10-fold cross-validation
  runs = 5
  )
# Outputting the cross-validation results
print(cv.results.bic)
```

```{r}
# Fitting the network structure using hill-climbing and AIC
all.aic.net <- hc(heartdisease.all, score = "aic")
# Fitting the connection probabilities
all.bn.aic <- bn.fit(all.aic.net, data = heartdisease.all, method = "bayes", 
                     iss = 2)
# Fitting the network structure using hill-climbing and BIC
all.bic.net <- hc(heartdisease.all, score = "bic")
# Fitting the connection probabilities
all.bn.bic <- bn.fit(all.bic.net, data = heartdisease.all, method = "bayes", 
                     iss = 2)
```

```{r}
library(Rgraphviz)
```

```{r}
# Plotting the network that used the AIC for structure fitting
graphviz.plot(all.aic.net)
```

```{r}
# Plotting the network that used the BIC for structure fitting
graphviz.plot(all.bic.net)
```

```{r}
library(gRain)
```

```{r}
junction <- as.grain(all.bn.bic)
# Compiling all network probabilities as a query grain
# Getting the estimated probabilities of the target variable (P(Target))
querygrain(junction, nodes = "target")$target
```

```{r}
# Checking if target and fastting blood sugar variables are d-seperated
dsep(all.bn.bic, "target", "fasting.blood.sugar")
```


```{r}
# Setting the evidence of fasting blood sugar being "Less than 120"
jblood.sugar.less <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "fasting.blood.sugar", 
                                 states = "Less than 120")
# P(target | fasting.blood.sugar = Less than 120)
querygrain(jblood.sugar.less, nodes = "target")$target
```

```{r}
# Setting the evidence of fasting blood sugar being "Greater than 120"
jblood.sugar.greater <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "fasting.blood.sugar", 
                                    states = "Greater than 120")
# P(target | fasting.blood.sugar = Greater than 120)
querygrain(jblood.sugar.greater, nodes = "target")$target
```

```{r}
# Getting the probabilities associated with resting bp s variable
querygrain(junction, nodes = "resting.bp.s")$resting.bp.s
```


```{r}
# P(resting.bp.s | fasting.blood.sugar = Less than 120)
querygrain(jblood.sugar.less, nodes = "resting.bp.s")$resting.bp.s
```

```{r}
# P(resting.bp.s | fasting.blood.sugar = Greater than 120)
querygrain(jblood.sugar.greater, nodes = "resting.bp.s")$resting.bp.s
```

```{r}
# Empty vector to store probabilities
probs.hd.age <- c()
# Storing the levels of the age variable
ages <- levels(heartdisease.all$age)
# Looping through each level of age
for (age in ages){
  # Setting the evidence of the current level of age
  j.age <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "age", states = age)
  # Outputting the result
  print(paste0("P(Target| age = ", age, ")"))
  # P(target | age = Current level)
  print(querygrain(j.age, nodes = "target")$target)
  # Storing P(target = Heart disease| age = Current level)
  probs.hd.age <- c(probs.hd.age, as.numeric(querygrain(j.age, 
                                                nodes = "target")$target[1]))
}
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r}
# Plotting a line graph of age level and probability of having heart disease
# Conditioned on it
ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = c(2:7), y = probs.hd.age)) + geom_line(color = 
"blue") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:6, labels=c("20s", "30s", "40s", 
                                                  "50s", "60s", "70s")) + 
  labs(x = "Age", y = "P(target = Heartdisease | age = x)", 
       title = "Probability of a patient having heart disease conditioned on 
       their age") + 
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(color = "blue"))
```

```{r}
# Empty vector to store probabilities
probs.hd.oldpeak = c()
# Storing the levels of oldpeak variable
oldpeaks <- levels(heartdisease.all$oldpeak)
# Looping through each level
for (oldpeak in oldpeaks){
  # Setting the evidence of oldpeak with current level
  j.oldpeak <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "oldpeak", states = oldpeak)
  # Outputting the results
  print(paste0("P(Target| oldpeak = ", oldpeak, ")"))
  # P(Target | oldpeak = Current level)
  print(querygrain(j.oldpeak, nodes = "target")$target)
  # Storing P(Target = heart disease | oldpeak = Current level)
  probs.hd.oldpeak <- c(probs.hd.oldpeak, as.numeric(querygrain(j.oldpeak, 
                                                nodes = "target")$target[1]))
  # Storing P(Target = Normal | oldpeak = Current level)
  probs.hd.oldpeak <- c(probs.hd.oldpeak, as.numeric(querygrain(j.oldpeak, 
                                                nodes = "target")$target[2]))
}
# Creating an indicator for oldpeak
oldpeak.indicator <- c("High", "High", "Normal", "Normal")
# Combining probabilities and indicators storing as a data frame
probs.hd.oldpeak.df <- as.data.frame(cbind(probs.hd.oldpeak, oldpeak.indicator))
```

```{r}
# Plotting the oldpeak and heart disease probabilities
ggplot() + geom_col(data = probs.hd.oldpeak.df, aes(x = c("Heart disease", 
                                                          "Normal", "Heart disease", 
                                                          "Normal"), 
                                                    y = probs.hd.oldpeak, 
                                                    fill = oldpeak.indicator),
                    position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Oldpeak", y = "P(target | oldpeak = x)", 
       title = "Probability of a patient having or not having heart disease conditioned on 
       their oldpeak") + guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Oldpeak")) + 
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(color = "blue"))
```

```{r}
# Empty vector to store probabilities
probs.hd.ST.slope <- c()
# Storing the levels of ST slope variable
ST.slopes <- levels(heartdisease.all$ST.slope)
# Looping through each level
for (ST.slope in ST.slopes){
  # Setting the evidence of ST slope being current level
  j.ST.slope <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "ST.slope", states = ST.slope)
  # Outputting P(Target | ST.slope = current level)
  print(paste0("P(Target| ST.slope = ", ST.slope, ")"))
  print(querygrain(j.ST.slope, nodes = "target")$target)
  # Storing P(Target = Heart disease | ST.slope = current level)
  probs.hd.ST.slope <- c(probs.hd.ST.slope, as.numeric(querygrain(j.ST.slope, 
                                                  nodes = "target")$target[1]))
  # Storing P(Target = Normal | ST.slope = current level)
  probs.hd.ST.slope <- c(probs.hd.ST.slope, as.numeric(querygrain(j.ST.slope, 
                                                  nodes = "target")$target[2]))
}
# Indicator for ST.slope
ST.slope.indicator <- c("Downsloping", "Downsloping", "Flat", "Flat", 
                        "Upsloping", "Upsloping")
# Storing conditional probabilities as data frame
probs.hd.ST.slope.df <- as.data.frame(cbind(probs.hd.ST.slope, 
                                            ST.slope.indicator))

```

```{r}
# Plotting the ST.slope and heart disease probabilities
ggplot() + geom_col(data = probs.hd.ST.slope.df, aes(x = c("Heart disease", 
                                                          "Normal", 
                                                          "Heart disease", 
                                                          "Normal",
                                                          "Heart disease",
                                                          "Normal"), 
                                                     y = probs.hd.ST.slope, 
          fill = ST.slope.indicator), position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "ST.slope", y = "P(target | ST.slope = x)", 
       title = "Probability of a patient having or not having heart 
       disease conditioned on 
       their ST.slope") + guides(fill=guide_legend(title="ST.slope")) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "black", "red")) + 
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(color = "blue"))
```

```{r}
# Calculating P(Sex)
querygrain(junction, nodes = "sex")$sex
```


```{r}
probs.hd.target <- c()
# Storing the levels of the target variable
targets <- levels(heartdisease.all$target)
# Looping through the levels
for (target in targets){
  # Setting the evidence of the target variable with current level
  j.target <- setEvidence(junction, nodes = "target", states = target)
  # Outputting the results
  print(paste0("P(Sex| Target = ", target, ")"))
  # P(sex | target = Current level)
  print(querygrain(j.target, nodes = "sex")$sex)
  # Storing P(sex = Female | target = x)
  probs.hd.target <- c(probs.hd.target, as.numeric(querygrain(j.target, 
                                                nodes = "sex")$sex[1]))
  # Storing P(sex = Male | target = x)
  probs.hd.target <- c(probs.hd.target, as.numeric(querygrain(j.target, 
                                                nodes = "sex")$sex[2]))
}
# Indicator for sex variable
target.indicator <- c("Heart disease", "Heart disease", "Normal", "Normal")
# Storing probabilities as a data frame
probs.hd.target.df <- as.data.frame(cbind(probs.hd.target, target.indicator))
```

```{r}
# Plotting the probabilities of sex conditioned on target
ggplot() + geom_col(data = probs.hd.target.df, aes(x = c("Female", 
                                                         "Male", 
                                                   "Female", "Male"), 
                                             y = probs.hd.target, fill = 
                                               target.indicator), position = 
                      "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Target", y = "P(sex | target = x)", 
       title = "Probability of a patient being a sex conditioned on target") +
  guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Target")) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(color = "blue"))
```

```{r}
# Data set excluding all possible outliers and excluding the outlier
# indicator
heartdisease.sub <- heartdisease.final[heartdisease.final$outlier == "No",-13]
```

```{r}
# Cross validation
cv.results.aic <- bn.cv(
  # Data set used
  data = heartdisease.sub,
  # Hill climbing algorithm is being used
  bn = "hc",
  # Scoring for the hill climbing algorithm is AIC
  algorithm.args = list(score = "aic"),
  # Probability fit type (Bayesian)
  fit = "bayes",
  # How much influence the prior has on the fitted probability
  fit.args = list(iss = 2),
  # Loss function for the cross validation (log-likelihood)
  loss =  "logl",
  # Number of folds
  k = 10,
  # Number of times to  repeat the 10-fold cross-validation
  runs = 5
)
# Outputting the results
print(cv.results.aic)
```

```{r}
# Cross validation
cv.results.bic <- bn.cv(
  # Data set used
  data = heartdisease.sub,
  # Hill climbing algorithm is being used
  bn = "hc",
  # Scoring for the hill climbing algorithm is BIC
  algorithm.args = list(score = "bic"),
  # Probability fit type (Bayesian)
  fit = "bayes",
  # How much influence the prior has on the fitted probability
  fit.args = list(iss = 2),
  # Loss function for the cross validation (log-likelihood)
  loss =  "logl",
  # Number of folds
  k = 10,
  # Number of times to  repeat the 10-fold cross-validation
  runs = 5
)
# Outputting the results
print(cv.results.bic)
```

```{r}
# Fitting the AIC scoring hill climbing algorithm
subset.aic.net <- hc(heartdisease.sub, score = "aic")
# Estimating the probabilities using a Bayesian approach
subset.bn.bde <- bn.fit(all.aic.net, data = heartdisease.all, method = "bayes", 
                        iss = 2)
# Fitting the BIC scoring hill climbing algorithm
subset.bic.net <- hc(heartdisease.sub, score = "bic")
# Estimating the probabilities using a Bayesian approach
subset.bn.bic <- bn.fit(all.bic.net, data = heartdisease.all, method = "bayes", 
                        iss = 2)
```

```{r}
# Plotting the AIC scoring network
graphviz.plot(subset.aic.net)
```
